proposals.title: Integrated Spatial-Expression Latent Embedding and Domain Detection
proposals.summary: This analysis implements a joint latent embedding that fuses spatial coordinates with gene expression data to detect biologically meaningful tissue domains. The approach builds a multi-scale spatial neighborhood graph and applies integrated dimensionality reduction, ensuring that both molecular details and spatial context are maintained. Comparative analyses against expression-only baselines are incorporated to demonstrate improvements in domain delineation and preservation of local heterogeneity.

proposals.title: Weighted Normalization with Expression-Only Benchmarking
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on robust quality control and dropout-aware normalization that balances both noisy expression and spatial variability. By applying weighted dimensionality reduction, the workflow explicitly benchmarks its integrated approach against traditional expression-only models. Sensitivity analyses are performed on weighting parameters to address the trade-off between oversmoothing and noise, ensuring that the integration enhances signal recovery.

proposals.title: Multi-scale Spatial Graph Construction and Oversmoothing Trade-off Analysis
proposals.summary: This proposal emphasizes the construction of a multi-scale spatial neighborhood graph that carefully tunes spatial smoothing. The analysis systematically evaluates the oversmoothing versus noise trade-off, using quantitative metrics and spatial autocorrelation measures. Comparisons to expression-only pipelines help validate that the chosen parameters minimize noise without blurring key tissue boundaries and rare cellular states.

proposals.title: Scalable Embedding and Domain Segmentation for Large Tissue Datasets
proposals.summary: Targeting the challenges of high-resolution spatial assays, this analysis develops a computational pipeline optimized for scalability. It integrates spatial and expression data into a compact latent space, effectively clustering large numbers of tissue locations. Scalability is benchmarked through runtime and memory profiling, while cross-validation against histological landmarks confirms the robustness of domain segmentation in large datasets.

proposals.title: Dropout-Aware Joint Integration for Expression Denoising and Domain Recovery
proposals.summary: This workflow prioritizes the recovery of true biological signals by addressing the prevalent dropout issues in spatial transcriptomics. It employs dropout-aware normalization followed by joint embedding of spatial and expression profiles to denoise signal. Differential expression analysis and domain validation steps are directly compared with results from expression-only methods, demonstrating improved reconstruction of underlying molecular gradients and tissue architecture.

proposals.title: Trajectory Inference in Integrated Latent Spaces with Spatial Continuity Checks
proposals.summary: Beyond discrete domain detection, this analysis extends the framework to capture continuous tissue transitions via trajectory inference. The method leverages the integrated latent space that arrives from balanced spatial and molecular features, applying continuity checks to ensure that inferred trajectories reflect true biological gradients rather than oversmoothed artifacts. Comparison with expression-only trajectory models highlights the added value of spatial context.

proposals.title: Sensitivity Analysis and Parameter Tuning for Robust Cross-Platform Integration
proposals.summary: Focusing on robust performance across diverse spatial platforms, this proposal introduces extensive sensitivity analyses on key parameters governing spatial connectivity and expression capture. The pipeline is refined to ensure that the integration of spatial and molecular data remains effective despite differences in resolution and noise levels across platforms. Comparative validations against expression-only pipelines further reinforce its cross-platform robustness.

proposals.title: Benchmarking Integrated Reconstruction and Denoising Against Expression-Only Baselines
proposals.summary: This analysis centers on a rigorous benchmarking framework that quantitatively compares the performance of the integrated spatial-expression method with traditional expression-only reconstruction pipelines. Emphasis is placed on metrics for expression denoising, recovery of dropout-obscured genes, and the ability to preserve spatial gradients. Detailed evaluation protocols including differential expression and landmark-based assessments ensure that the integrated approach significantly outperforms conventional methods in restoring true biological signals.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly eight computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, via a three-step draft–critique–synthesis workflow producing JSON artifacts at specified paths.

steps.title: Draft proposal set with spatial_cv_agent
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to generate an initial JSON draft of candidate computational spatial-omics analyses, informed only by the provided background on spatially aware latent representations, neighborhood graphs, and downstream tasks (e.g., domain detection, denoising, reconstruction, cross-platform use). The agent should write this draft as a structured set of proposed analyses—without executing them—to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`.
steps.reasoning: This step leverages a spatially focused planning agent to translate the conceptual problem (learning compact spatial–expression representations and evaluating them) into a coherent set of candidate analysis proposals; it anchors the entire workflow by producing a concrete, machine-readable draft artifact that later agents can critique and refine.
steps.assignment_rationale: The spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required for this TA+CV treatment and is specialized for drafting spatial-paper analyses, writing the draft proposals to project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json.

steps.title: Critique draft proposals using Critic agent
steps.description: Have a Critic-style agent read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and assess the draft proposals for coverage of key goals (spatial–expression integration, avoidance of over-smoothing, comparison to expression-only baselines, scalability, reconstruction of noisy expression, and cross-platform robustness), as well as clarity, distinctness, and feasibility as computational analyses. The agent should record structured comments and improvement suggestions—again without defining new proposals or running analyses—in `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique step ensures that the eventual eight proposals are not just plausible but also well-aligned with the stated challenges and typical evaluation axes of spatial representation learning; encoding this feedback in a separate JSON artifact creates a clear input for the final synthesis step.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is dedicated to review and critique, and is the only agent that writes project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json without generating new proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final eight proposals from feedback
steps.description: Use a final-synthesis/Hypothesis-style agent to combine the initial draft (`project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json`) and its critique (`project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`) into a single, polished set of exactly eight distinct computational spatial-omics analyses that the hidden paper is most likely to have performed. The agent must write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly eight items, each of which has only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the analysis conceptually (without executing it).
steps.reasoning: This synthesis step operationalizes the critique to refine, merge, or adjust the draft ideas into a finalized, non-redundant set of eight proposals that collectively address the representation-learning and evaluation challenges described in the background, while conforming strictly to the required JSON structure for the benchmark.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is designed for final synthesis of spatial-paper analyses and is the appropriate agent to produce project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json with exactly eight polished proposal entries.

provenance.justification: Available templates focus on executing specific biological or spatial analyses or on multi-step paper-hypothesis generation workflows with many artifacts, whereas this task is a tightly constrained three-step meta-planning and proposal-synthesis pipeline that must produce only the specified JSON files; therefore, the plan was constructed from scratch to respect the benchmark’s structure and artifact requirements.
